subject: AstraNova committed capacity & p95 latency headroom modeling
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@astranova.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: AstraNova committed capacity planning: rough numbers attached

Marcus —

Thanks for taking a look. We're preparing a committed capacity proposal for an initial product launch (Q3) and want to validate whether Redwood Dedicated can meet our throughput and p95 latency targets. Attached is a traffic profile export from our staging workload (astranova_usage_profile.xlsx). High-level ask below: 

- Expected steady-state: ~3.5M tokens/day (spiky distribution)
- Peak concurrency: 120 concurrent requests during 10% of traffic windows
- Average request size: 400 tokens in, 1200 tokens out (generation-heavy)
- Target SLO: p95 inference latency <= 350ms for interactive generates

Can you provide a ballpark dedicated-slab recommendation (GPU count / slab sizing), tokens/sec mapping, and suggested headroom assumptions? Also call out fallback strategies if we need to degrade to smaller models to preserve latency.

Would like a short write-up ahead of a call next week.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of ML Infrastructure | AstraNova

Attachments: astranova_usage_profile.xlsx (traffic export)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@astranova.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-05T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: AstraNova committed capacity planning: rough numbers attached

Elena —

Thanks, received the profile. I did a quick pass and attached a compact estimate (initial_compute_estimate.csv) with conservative assumptions. A few clarifying Qs so we can tighten the numbers before the call: 

1) Concurrency pattern: is the 120 concurrent requests mostly sustained for the 10% peak windows, or are they short microbursts?
2) Streaming vs non-streaming: what fraction of requests will use streaming token-by-token responses? Streaming materially increases p95 tail complexity.
3) Acceptable error for p95: is 350ms a hard cutoff or a commercial target (i.e., acceptable with 10% soft exceedance)?

Prelim highlights from our side: 
- Using the profile and assuming mixed streaming (30%) and non-streaming (70%), the workload maps to ~24–28 tokens/sec sustained per slab for your chosen model family (fp16/resnet-like kernels).
- To meet p95 <= 350ms under the reported request sizes, we recommend planning for ~2x nominal capacity headroom on top of steady-state to handle the 10% peak windows without queueing. That maps to ~6 dedicated slabs (N=6) as a starting point; we can tighten after you confirm concurrency burst characteristics.

I'll loop in Irene for a short SLO-fit matrix (tokens/sec -> p95) and a fallback model suggestion. Ben/Naomi: flagged for cost sensitivity and deal packaging.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachment: initial_compute_estimate.csv
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@astranova.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-05T13:30:00Z
Subject: Re: AstraNova committed capacity planning: rough numbers attached

Elena / team —

I dug into the profile Marcus attached and ran a Monte Carlo-style headroom simulation based on your token distribution and request-size mix. Summary (short):

- Baseline mapping: steady-state tokens/sec requirement = ~580 tps aggregated. This assumes 3.5M tokens/day smoothed over peak windows.
- Model perf: for your target model (approx. 15–20B parameter class, expected inference profile): per-GPU sustained throughput = ~22–30 tps depending on sequence packing and KV-cache reuse. We used a conservative 24 tps for planning.
- SLO fit: p95 <= 350ms is achievable at 24 tps/GPU only if average request concurrency per-GPU stays <= 8 and streaming fraction is <= 35%. If streaming > 50% we observe p95 growth due to long-tail stalls (KV cache warmups + small-batch inefficiencies).

Recommendation (deal-specific commitment plan):
- Committed slabs: 6 slabs (each slab = 8 GPUs) mapped to your region. This yields nominal capacity ~24 tps/GPU * 48 GPUs = ~1,152 tps headroom at slab level and ~2x steady-state cushion vs reported average.
- Burst policy: enable Dedicated burst into shared capacity for short microbursts (up to +50% for 5–10 minute windows) — contractually capped.
- Fallbacks: automatic model switch to a quantized 8-bit variant for non-critical requests (saves ~35% GPU cycles) and a lightweight 7B model for interactive endpoints if observed p95 drift > 20% for 15+ minutes.
- Ops playbook: warm key-value caches on deploys, pre-warm frequent prefixes during your daily peak window, and set request-level timeouts at 4s to surface degradations.

Cost/packaging note (Ben/Naomi): with a 12-month reserved commit at the 6-slab level we can propose a blended unit price that includes surge credits for the first three months while traffic stabilizes. I'll attach the modeling PDF and a short simulation summary.

Next steps: Marcus/Elena — if you can confirm whether peak concurrency is sustained or bursty and the expected streaming fraction, we'll finalize slab count and draft the SLR (service-level requirements) for legal/procurement.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Staff Technical Program Manager, Inference Optimization | Redwood Inference

Attachments: astranova_headroom_model.pdf; simulation_results_summary.txt
From: Elena Park <elena@astranova.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Timothy Cole <tim.cole@astranova.ai>
Date: 2028-05-05T16:48:00Z
Subject: Re: AstraNova committed capacity planning: rough numbers attached

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick replies inline: 

- Concurrency pattern: 95% of the time the 120 concurrent is a sustained plateau across our US peak window (about 30–45 minutes), not millisecond microbursts.
- Streaming fraction: ~25% of requests; most user-facing flows return token-by-token progress for UX.
- p95 tolerance: 350ms is a hard target for primary interactive flows; background batch jobs can tolerate higher latency.

We'll aim to accept the 6-slab plan subject to a short on-site calibration POC (1 week) to validate p95 under realistic traffic. I'll coordinate with ProcureOps to get draft SLR language and cost expectations. Can we schedule a 30-min tech-runthrough early next week?
